gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Big, loud, and spread out. Noto Sans Ethiopic follows as a plain sans with sturdy tall lowercase, so Paprika's hollow-reed counters get the spotlight while the text stays steady underneath.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals. Noto Sans Georgian sits beneath as a plain sans with open curves and short ascender stems, giving that heavy display voice a modern, tidy partner.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Paprika scatters its letters wide, and its lowercase stretches to fill the line like capitals. Noto Sans Glagolitic does the opposite job, with round, open shapes that stay clear at small sizes in sturdy sans-serif form.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Commanding is how Paprika comes across, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open. And Noto Sans Gothic handles the quieter work, its big glass-bead counters and round parenthesis-like forms staying easy to follow.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha is a professional sans-serif with tall, compact letters, like pen-nib bowls pressed flat. Noto Sans Grantha keeps a long stretch of text moving smoothly, since no closed-up bowl ever catches the eye.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Expressive from the first letter, Paprika spaces its forms out and lets each lowercase shape fill the line. And Noto Sans Gujarati, a clean plain sans with large open counters, gives that loud heading a tall, tidy partner.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gond: Commanding, with letters scattered wide, Paprika leads the way. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi follows as a plain sans with crayon-tall strokes and terminals cut back to leave a big gap, which keeps the page contemporary.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads clean and tidy, with outward-pointing terminals. Its low ascenders, barely clearing the x-height, sit neatly under Paprika's wide-set, line-filling lowercase, and that sharp difference in scale is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Loud, wide, and full of presence, Paprika scatters its letters and lets lowercase fill the line like capitals. Noto Sans Hebrew, a modern sans-serif, calms things below.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-hk: Paprika's hollow-reed counters and line-filling lowercase are what you notice first. But Noto Sans HK, a clean sans with large lowercase forms and lifted brush ends, does the quieter job of carrying the text.
